# PC fracture meshes on mobile

These assets are an offline export of this project's existing PC `CombatV2/fracture_v2.fbx`, placed using `combat-assets.json` and the centred parent transforms in `SourceAssets/assets.json`. The public repository provides the complete runtime export; original PC/Blender authoring inputs and export scripts are not included. The fragment mesh data does not use substituted rubble models or copied third-party mesh assets. Applied environment and architectural textures have their own CC0 attribution records.

- 3,337 structural fragments and 2,296 glass fragments, 5,633 total, owned by the same 48 sectors as the intact mobile building.
- 194,181 triangles after mobile LOD, comprising 175,813 structural triangles and 18,368 glass triangles. The source has 652,537 triangles across 3,425 unique meshes; the 88 glass template meshes are instantiated for all 287 panes.
- Each structural fragment retains inclined fracture caps. All glass pieces retain the original closed triangular prism: six positions, eight triangles, and real pane thickness.
- Structural LOD dissolves coplanar faces within 0.001 radians, preserving material borders, then uses 0.25 collapse on complex meshes. Collapse is rejected if it removes a connected component or material, adds boundary edges, or shifts any fragment bound more than 15 mm. 1,258 collapse operations were accepted and 105 rejected. This reduces surface detail while preserving every fragment and source component.
- Maximum original parent bounds difference is 13.85 mm; maximum 48-sector bounds difference is 16.60 mm. The intact mobile mesh has its own earlier simplification, so its bounds are not numerically identical to the PC source. Original fragment placement before LOD matched PC parent bounds within 1 micrometre.
- Positions are local to each fragment's world AABB centre, in metres. Rest world coordinates convert Blender `(x,y,z)` to Three `(x,z,-y)`. `partId` follows the original lab manifest's floor/cell grouping, matching the intact mobile exporter. The centred PC parent position is distinct from the original lab root position; using the latter for placement would misalign the fragments.
- Existing architectural colours come from `optimize-assets-v2.palette`, encoded as linear normalized unsigned bytes. Source UVs and normals accompany the geometry. LOD preserves surviving UV corner values, with interpolation across simplified surfaces.
- `pc-fragments.bin` is 22,719,180 bytes, uncompressed, and has five separately aligned buffers: float32 positions, float32 normals, float32 UVs, normalized uint8 RGB colours, and float32 piece indices. JSON offsets are bytes; lengths are component counts. Structure and glass occupy contiguous `materialRanges` measured in vertices.
- The complete build exceeds the initial 25 MB distribution goal because the unchanged intact GLB is already 8.10 MB. This version keeps the straightforward uncompressed contract and does not introduce a new browser decompression dependency.

The JSON `provenance` retains the original input hashes, relative source identifiers, coordinate rules, topology guard statistics, and measured bounds errors. Historical script names and source paths identify the offline export; they are not required local paths for running this repository. To replace the exported data, preserve the documented binary and JSON contracts and run `tests/fragment-assets.test.cjs`. The original architecture includes nonmanifold construction seams; this export does not claim to repair those existing seams, and introduces no new boundary edges.

Validation: `node --test tests/fragment-assets.test.cjs` checks binary layout, all 5,633 source instances, all 48 owners, finite UVs/positions, normalized normals, local bounds, original source identifiers, inclined concrete caps on every structural fragment, and watertight outward glass prisms. Browser visual acceptance and device frame rate remain separate runtime checks.
